recorded.prompt:q-jit:b: Read the page and each keyed question. For every wrong option, say whether a passage of the page rules it out, and quote or name that passage.
recorded.pass:q-jit:b: an independent reader (19-concurrency-pitfalls q3), never the author
recorded.outcome:q-jit:b: ruled out: README_5.3.3.md explicitly states hardware keeps caches coherent: "(CPU caches are kept coherent by the hardware; the usual culprit for a read that never updates is the JIT.)"
recorded.prompt:q-jit:c: Read the page and each keyed question. For every wrong option, say whether a passage of the page rules it out, and quote or name that passage.
recorded.pass:q-jit:c: an independent reader (19-concurrency-pitfalls q3), never the author
recorded.outcome:q-jit:c: ruled out: The page says the interpreter behaves the opposite way: "In interpreted mode (-Xint), visibility bugs may not manifest because the JVM reads from main memory on every access. Once the JIT compiles the method, it may hoist loop-invariant reads into registers." It is the JIT after warm-up, not the interpreter, that causes stale reads.
recorded.prompt:q-tearing:a: Read the page and each keyed question. For every wrong option, say whether a passage of the page rules it out, and quote or name that passage.
recorded.pass:q-tearing:a: an independent reader (19-concurrency-pitfalls q3), never the author
recorded.outcome:q-tearing:a: ruled out: The page repeatedly states volatile does not make compound operations atomic, e.g. Key Points: "guarantees visibility of the most recent write for a single variable ... but does NOT provide atomicity for compound operations like i++", and the VolatileCounterBug example: "count++; // Read (volatile), add 1, write (volatile) -- 3 non-atomic steps!"
recorded.prompt:q-tearing:c: Read the page and each keyed question. For every wrong option, say whether a passage of the page rules it out, and quote or name that passage.
recorded.pass:q-tearing:c: an independent reader (19-concurrency-pitfalls q3), never the author
recorded.outcome:q-tearing:c: ruled out: The page describes volatile as forcing a fresh read from memory rather than serving from a register -- the FixedFlag example says "while (!stop) { // Volatile read on every iteration -- always sees latest value }", the opposite of a register-served, faster access; the register-caching described elsewhere is precisely the non-volatile bug volatile avoids.
